clue.text: Actor Bill has rejected scriptwriter's material, companion admitted to Al

indicators.note: admitted to means the pieces before it are let inside the word standing for Al

parts.note: Al Jolson was the American singer and star of The Jazz Singer
AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: rejected means the word for the writer's material is turned back to front

parts.note: ink is what a writer of script puts on the page
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A performer named Bill turns down a writer's pages while a friend is let in to see someone called Al.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Al' is a person, the singer of The Jazz Singer, not a word to be read as letters; 'rejected' turns the writer's material backwards before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named is a celebrated Hollywood film star, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: King Edward, perhaps, supporting shilling as old coin

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the potato word comes after the shilling letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling
King Edward is a variety of potato, and tater is slang for potato

explanation.surface: A British monarch is pictured propping up a shilling, as if on an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece, so it is an old piece of money.

clue.text: Distribution of letters in cinematography wasn't witless with 1 24 across

indicators.note: the letters in the following words are dealt out afresh, as a mail carrier distributes letters

explanation.surface: Someone praises a film's camera work as anything but dull, mentioning its star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of letters in' rearranges CINEMATOGRAPHY WASNT WITLESS, twenty-six letters, into the five-word title; it also hints at the mail carrier of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1981 thriller starred the actor named at 1 24 across, so it is a film made with him.

clue.text: Not exactly partial to mints or toffees

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are only somewhat keen on sweets like mints or toffees.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial hedge meaning roughly or more or less, the same as not exactly.

clue.text: Old craft, given variable energy, flower power doubled up

parts.note: Z is a letter used for a variable in algebra
E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a flower is a river, something that flows; the Nile is one

indicators.note: doubled means the letter for power is written twice

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: An old vessel gets fuelled by changing energy, and the flower power movement is lifted twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (something that flows), not a bloom; 'up' turns the river plus the doubled power letter, read from the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship of the early twentieth century, an old type of flying craft.

clue.text: Overcook fish

definitions.meaning: to ... food is to scorch or blacken it by cooking too long
a fish of the salmon family found in cold lakes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to scorch something on the heat and a trout-like freshwater fish.

clue.text: Famed ego now damaged with 1 24 across

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the preceding words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity's pride has been hurt, as noted alongside a star actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges FAMEDEGONOW into the four-word film title.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1992 courtroom drama starred the actor named at 1 24 across, so it is a film made with him.

clue.text: Fish, survivor of the 16th century?

definitions.meaning: Catherine ... was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and outlived him

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a young salmon and the surname of the Tudor queen who survived her husband Henry VIII.

clue.text: Wasted the bacon sandwiches I cut

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the bacon sandwiches that they cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' puts I inside THE BACON, and 'Wasted' rearranges the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a butcher's cut of beef from the rump bone, so it is a cut of meat.

clue.text: Character on rugby field, ancient king with 1 24 across

parts.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H
Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia in England

explanation.surface: A personality on a rugby pitch, an old monarch, and a famous actor share the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby goalposts form a giant H on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1992 biopic of a union boss starred the actor named at 1 24 across, so it is a film made with him.

clue.text: Equip with central part in future to stop crash

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the middle letters go inside the word for crash

parts.note: to crash is to sleep, and kip is British slang for sleep

indicators.note: central part in picks the middle letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Fitting something with a key component should prevent accidents later.
explanation.walkthrough: KIP is British slang for a sleep; 'crash' is informal for sleeping, not a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit up is to fit out with clothing or gear, which is to equip someone.

clue.text: Very best main attraction?

definitions.meaning: of the highest quality or class
read as ..., the thing that draws people most, a star attraction

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means first-rate, and cryptically also something that draws the biggest crowd.

clue.text: Honeybunch and sweetie-pie, say, with 1 24 across

definitions.meaning: these are affectionate pet names, examples of loving forms of address
the 1983 film starring the actor named at 1 24 across

explanation.definitionFit: Affectionate nicknames are loving forms of address, and the phrase is also the title of a 1983 Oscar-winning film.

clue.text: See 3
Take it easy, if copyright of song is yours!

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
if something is yours you own it; here the copyright of the song is yours

explanation.surface: Someone is told to relax if they hold the rights to a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copyright of' is a link telling you the song belongs to you; LIED is the German word for song used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to rest or relax, which is to take it easy.

clue.text: See 13 across
Relative English written in French resort

indicators.note: written in means the abbreviation is placed inside the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A family member's name appears in a French holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relative.

clue.text: I love to get stuck into stupid dialect

indicators.note: to get stuck into means the letter for love is pushed inside the word for stupid

parts.note: dim means stupid
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone wants to tackle an awkward regional way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom can mean a dialect or a characteristic form of speech, as in the local idiom.

clue.text: In fall, southern leaves blue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaves means the letter goes away from the word for fall

parts.note: a descent is a fall or drop

explanation.surface: In autumn the leaves of the south are melancholy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' and 'leaves' suggest autumn trees and 'blue' sadness; in fact S departs from DESCENT and blue means rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are smutty or obscene, so blue means indecent.

clue.text: See 7
I'm upset, given nothing special, having finished Japanese food

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: so-so means mediocre, nothing special
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A diner is disappointed that a mediocre meal is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso soup is a Japanese broth made from fermented soybean paste, a staple Japanese dish.

clue.text: Duck died, strangled by old magistrate

indicators.note: strangled by means the abbreviation is held tight inside the word for the magistrate

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice or Genoa

explanation.surface: A duck has been killed by an elderly judge wringing its neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a bird; it is the verb, to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to evade or avoid something, which is to dodge it.

clue.text: University to take off unsigned forms, they conclude

indicators.note: forms means the remaining letters are made into a new shape
to take off means the letter is removed from the following word

explanation.surface: A university decides to remove forms that nobody has signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take off' removes U from UNSIGNED, and 'forms' rearranges NSIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Endings are the final parts of something, the things that conclude it.

clue.text: Transport by cart, say, always 'ard in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means
ay, or aye, is an old word for always
the dropped aitch of hard, written as given

explanation.surface: Moving goods by cart is said to be always hard going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns EG + AY + ARD into DRAYAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a cart, and drayage is the moving of goods by dray, so carriage by cart.

clue.text: End cut from waste pipe filling European river

indicators.note: filling means the shortened pipe goes inside the word for European

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

indicators.note: cut from means the following word's letters are removed from the pipe

parts.note: a U-bend is the curved waste pipe under a sink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken drain fitting spills into a big river of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A U-bend is the curved waste pipe under a sink; 'End' gives its own letters, which 'cut from' removes before the remainder fills the European.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major river flowing through central and eastern Europe.

clue.text: See 3
See 1
One squealing, as upset

definitions.meaning: a police informer, one who squeals
British slang for to annoy or irritate

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for an informer and also a verb meaning to irritate or anger.

clue.text: Oven grill's surface wiped

indicators.note: surface wiped means the top letter is removed, the down light's surface being its first letter

parts.note: to toast is to grill; the 's is has

explanation.surface: The top of a cooker's grill gets cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the surface is the top letter, so T goes from TOAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven.

clue.text: Auditor's fashion cut

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what follows is how a word is heard

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A financial inspector's style has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; here it is a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mowed has been cut.

clue.text: Author held up one side

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: had means held
L is left, one side

explanation.surface: A writer is delayed while one side waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a writer of children's books, an author.

clue.text: See 3
Unlikely story, ancient spa harbouring new well!

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: harbouring means the spa town holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Bath is the English spa town
my! is an exclamation of surprise like well!

explanation.surface: An old spa town is said to hold a new well, a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the Roman spa city in Somerset, England; Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city that comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely told but untrue story, an unlikely tale.
